To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

digital games for physical therapy can be developed with currently available commercial off-the-shelf hardware and software, provided that the games are designed in such a way that calibration and adaptation are possible".

1) the calibration and adaptation of the game to the motor skills of the player can be done by using a combination of the input device and a simple calibration routine; 2) the game can be adapted to the player's goals by adjusting the game parameters; 3) the calibration and the adaptation are feasible with commercially available input devices; 4) the game can easily be extended by adding more minigames.
digital games can be used for physical therapy, but the game design should be tailored to the needs of the patient and the therapist.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of digital physical therapy games, and with the calibration and adaptation of the game to the user's needs.
the development of digital game minigames for the rehabilitation of people with motor disabilities.
the question how the input device can be used as a calibration tool for the player's actions and how this information can be used to adapt the game.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed games that are feasible for people suffering from severe spasticity and/or motor impairment.
the development of digital minigames for physical therapy is feasible with currently available commercial hardware and software.
the development of digital physical therapy games with currently available commercial off-the-shelf input devices is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of commercial game consoles, such as the Wii and Xbox 360, in combination with commercial input devices, such as the EyeToy camera, is feasible for the development of games for physical therapy.

we have shown that it is possible to develop digital games for people with disabilities that are fun to play, that can be adapted to the player's abilities, that are calibrated for the individual player and that can be used in a therapeutic setting.
the use of commercial input devices in the development of games for rehabilitation purposes is feasible, but that it is necessary to pay special attention to calibration and adaptation procedures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calibration of the games is crucial to make them accessible to people with motor disabilities, and that this can be done in a user-friendly way.
the use of digital games for rehabilitation is a promising area of research, but that the development of such games requires a multidisciplinary approach.
it is possible to create digital games for physical rehabilitation, which can be adapted to the player's needs, by means of calibration and parameter adjustment.
